title: Novak says fuel market 'partially stabilized' at Eastern Economic Forum, acknowledges lingering gasoline shortfall
detail: Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia's domestic market is now fully supplied with diesel and jet fuel, while gasoline still faces "a shortage at the moment, but it is small." He said the situation had "improved somewhat this week" after a number of refineries resumed operations and supplied additional volumes to the market, though minor shortages persist at filling stations in the Siberian and Ural federal districts, which he attributed to "purely a logistics issue." Novak said Russia has sufficient domestic capacity to repair 100% of its refineries without relying on imported equipment, and that the government will keep balancing the market through both higher domestic output and additional fuel imports from neighboring and other foreign markets.

media.caption: Deputy PM Alexander Novak briefs reporters on the domestic fuel market at the Eastern Economic Forum, Sept 3 2026
